answer: Each agent can post a bond that is locked for a long horizon and forfeited when independent audits show coordinated identities claiming separate rewards. Auditors sample linked accounts and compare their timing and behavior; a confirmed cluster loses its bonds, while honest agents recover theirs after the review window. This makes a sybil farm costly: the attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it all, rather than creating accounts for free. A saffron garden can be a shared test case, not proof of personhood.
